proportion.label: fashion
prompt_translation: Create a high-fashion nine-head visual proportion on a believable adult body: tall, elongated and elegant rather than anime-stretched.
Slightly reduce the head's visual share of the full figure while keeping face width, face shape and all identity geometry unchanged.
Keep the ribcage and torso fully developed; do not shorten the torso to create longer legs.
Lengthen the hip-to-knee and knee-to-ankle segments in balance, preserving natural knee position, pelvis width, ankle scale and foot proportion.
Raise the waistline only visually through sash placement, skirt-panel origin and vertical garment lines rather than compressing the anatomical torso.
Bias the costume toward vertical flow and slightly control sleeve/skirt lateral mass so the garment supports the tall fashion silhouette.

rules: Hair buns, crowns, hairpins and head ornaments do not count toward the visual head unit.
Never create a smaller-looking head by narrowing the face, enlarging the shoulders, or changing facial identity.
Head-scale correction must be achieved through whole-figure relationship and framing, not facial reshaping.
Do not lengthen only the thigh or only the calf.
Keep knee placement believable relative to pelvis and ankle.
Preserve natural pelvis width and realistic lower-limb soft tissue.
Do not enlarge the feet after elongating the figure.
Use sash placement, skirt-panel origin and long vertical panel lines to support a taller silhouette without changing garment identity.
Reduce only excess lateral sleeve/skirt spread; do not redesign the costume or remove signature layers.
Preserve enough footwear visibility to clarify the full vertical figure.

proportion.note: All head-count values are project visual heuristics, not vendor-native parameters or medical/anatomical measurements. Hair buns, crowns, hairpins and other head ornaments are excluded from the visual head unit.

human_presence.label: human_presence_refined
prompt_translation: Keep the locked face identity but give the cheeks, eyelids, nose wings, mouth corners and jaw-to-neck transition believable soft-tissue volume.

Use subtle regional skin response instead of one uniform polished surface: restrained forehead sheen, slightly stronger nose highlight, softer cheek diffusion, thinner eye-area response and independent lip material.
Allow extremely small natural asymmetries in brow height, eyelid openness, mouth-corner balance and highlight distribution without changing the character identity.
Make eye anatomy physically believable: natural eyeball-to-socket relationship, real upper/lower lid thickness, inner/outer canthus structure, integrated lash roots and non-pure-white sclera.
Build hair from primary masses, secondary strand groups and only a few fine irregular hairs, with non-uniform specular flow.
Use photographic highlight roll-off, preserved shadow detail, natural local micro-contrast and no global mathematical sharpness or edge halos.
soft_structure_rules: cheek soft tissue remains continuous with the original identity
nose wings have soft volume instead of hard modeled edges
jaw-to-neck transition is soft and anatomical rather than razor-sharp
micro_asymmetry_rules: never alter eye spacing, nose proportion, jaw geometry or overall face identity
lens_response_rules: face focus strongest but not digitally cut out
peripheral cloth can resolve slightly softer than the face
human_presence.principle: Beauty without CG: realism should come from soft structure, regional optics, small asymmetries, eye anatomy, hair irregularity and camera response rather than larger pores, aging cues or global sharpening.

round_plan.prompt_strategy: human-presence-only patch: soft structure + micro-asymmetry + eye/hair/lens realism while locking identity, P9 proportion and costume
